title: QuasiCoherentSymmetricAlgebraAffine
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and $S=P^\#$ the explicitly constructed symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction]. Then the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module of $S$ is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U$, the sheafification unit $\theta_U: \operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}F(U)\to S(U)$ is bijective.

source.place: Modules, Section 01CF (section-symmetric-exterior, line 3262: definition of Sym(F) as a quotient of the tensor algebra), Lemma 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra, line 3303: Sym^n F is the sheafification of U -> Sym^n_{O(U)}(F(U))), Lemma 01CL (lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence, line 3461: Sym of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent); Schemes, Section 01LA item (9) (schemes.tex line 4717); used as Sym^*_{O_X} in Properties, Lemmas 05JS, 086N, 0817

proof.text: *Step 4 (local setup on an affine open).* Fix an affine open $U\subseteq X$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$, $A=\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\mathcal P(U)$, and let $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ be the canonical open immersion with image $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]; via $\iota_U$ the opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are the opens of $X$ contained in $U$, and the affine opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are the affine opens of $X$ contained in $U$ (an open subscheme isomorphic to an affine scheme). These form a basis of $U$ (every open of a scheme is covered by affine opens: standard opens $D(g)$ of affine opens are affine and form a basis, Schemes, Lemma 01I3 and Algebra, Lemma 00E0). Let $\mathcal S=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ be the restriction of the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ along $\iota_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], so $\mathcal S(V)=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal S)=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)$ with its $R$-module structure through $\sigma_U$. Let $\widetilde A$ be the $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-module of the $R$-module $A$, with $\tau_V:A\to\widetilde A(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; it is quasi-coherent. The $R$-linear map $\theta_U:A\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal S)$ corresponds by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1) to a unique $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-linear $\alpha:\widetilde A\to\mathcal S$ with $\alpha_U\circ\tau_U=\theta_U$. For every affine open $V\subseteq U$, $\alpha_V\tau_V(a)=\alpha_V(\tau_U(a)|_V)=\alpha_U(\tau_U(a))|_V=\theta_U(a)|_V=\theta_V(\rho_{UV}(a))$ for $a\in A$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions: the mapping property of M~) and Section 01I6 (section-quasi-coherent-affine); route written by the agent

proof.text: *Step 5 (the sections over affine opens $V\subseteq U$, before sheafification).* Let $V\subseteq U$ be an affine open, $R_V=\mathcal O_X(V)$. (i) By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] for $\mathcal F$ (quasi-coherent) and $V\subseteq U$, the map $R_V\otimes_RM\to\mathcal F(V)$, $r\otimes m\mapsto r\,m|_V$, is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] (for $R\to R_V$) and this isomorphism, the $R_V$-algebra map $\lambda_V:R_V\otimes_RA\to\mathcal P(V)=\operatorname{Sym}_{R_V}(\mathcal F(V))$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\,\rho_{UV}(a)$, is bijective: indeed $\rho_{UV}$ is the $R$-algebra map with $\iota_U(m)\mapsto\iota_V(m|_V)$, i.e. Sym of $M\to R_V\otimes_RM\cong\mathcal F(V)$, $m\mapsto 1\otimes m$, so $\lambda_V$ is the isomorphism of that node composed with $\operatorname{Sym}_{R_V}$ of an isomorphism. (ii) By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] for the quasi-coherent $\widetilde A$ on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ (affine opens $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\widetilde A)=A$ via $\tau_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2)), the map $\beta_V:R_V\otimes_RA\to\widetilde A(V)$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\,\tau_V(a)$, is bijective. (iii) $\alpha_V\beta_V=\theta_V\lambda_V$: both are $R_V$-linear ($\alpha$ is $\mathcal O$-linear, $\theta_V$ is an $R_V$-algebra map) and agree on $1\otimes a$ by the last formula of Step 4. (iv) For affine opens $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ and $c\in R_V\otimes_RA$, with $c'$ the image of $c$ under $R_V\otimes A\to R_W\otimes A$ (restriction on the first factor): $\lambda_W(c')=\rho_{VW}(\lambda_V(c))$ and $\beta_W(c')=\beta_V(c)|_W$, since on $r\otimes a$ both sides are $r|_W\rho_{UW}(a)$, resp. $r|_W\tau_W(a)$ (restrictions of $\mathcal P$ and $\widetilde A$ are semilinear and $\rho_{VW}\rho_{UV}=\rho_{UW}$, $\tau_V(a)|_W=\tau_W(a)$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization: Sym commutes with localization, here in the base-change form) and Constructions, Lemma 01LN (sections of a quasi-coherent module over nested affines); route written by the agent

proof.text:
*Step 6 ($\alpha$ is an isomorphism).* Let $x\in U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](2) the underlying sheaf of abelian groups of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$, with $	heta$, is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal P$, so the map of stalks $	heta_x:\mathcal P_x	o\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)_x$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space]; the stalk of $\mathcal S$ at the point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ over $x$ is $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)_x$ (the neighbourhoods of $x$ inside $U$ are cofinal). Stalks are colimits over neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and affine opens $V
i x$ in $U$ are cofinal among them (Step 4). *$\alpha_x$ surjective:* a germ $t_x$, $t\in\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(V')$, is $	heta_x(p_x)$ with $p\in\mathcal P(W)$, $x\in W$; take an affine $V
i x$ with $V\subseteq W\cap U$ and $c=\lambda_V^{-1}(p|_V)$; then $t_x=(	heta_V\lambda_V(c))_x=(\alpha_V eta_V(c))_x=\alpha_x(( eta_V c)_x)$ by Step 5 (i),(iii). *$\alpha_x$ injective:* let $s\in\widetilde A(V')$ with $\alpha_x(s_x)=0$; take an affine $V
i x$ in $V'$ and $c= eta_V^{-1}(s|_V)$; then $	heta_x((\lambda_Vc)_x)=(\alpha_V eta_Vc)_x=0$, so $(\lambda_Vc)_x=0$ in $\mathcal P_x$, i.e. $\lambda_V(c)|_W=0$ for some affine $W
i x$, $W\subseteq V$; by Step 5 (iv) $\lambda_W(c')=0$, so $c'=0$ ($\lambda_W$ injective) and $s|_W= eta_V(c)|_W= eta_W(c')=0$, hence $s_x=0$. So $\alpha_x$ is bijective for every point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $\alpha:\widetilde A	o\mathcal S$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks].

proof.text: *Step 7 (conclusions: quasi-coherence and (b)).* Every point of $X$ lies in an affine open $U$ (definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]), and by Step 6 $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)|_U\cong\widetilde A$ for the $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module $A=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal F(U))$; so the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For (b): for every affine open $U$, $\theta_U=\alpha_U\tau_U$ (Step 4) with $\tau_U$ bijective [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2) and $\alpha_U$ bijective (Step 6), so $\theta_U:\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F(U))\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)$, which by Step 2 is the $R$-algebra map extending $j_{\mathcal F,U}$, is an isomorphism. (Stacks gets the quasi-coherence from Modules, Lemma 01CL, and the affine description from Schemes, Lemma 01I8(2), $\widetilde{\operatorname{Sym}^n(M)}\cong\operatorname{Sym}^n(\widetilde M)$, summed over $n$.)
